identity.title: The impact of a massive star cluster on its surrounding matter in the Antennae overlap region

paper_type_evidence.quote: We combine the previous dataset with archive observations done with the ALMA interferometer in the Cycle 0 early science process between July and November 2012
The data was retrieved from the ALMA science archive fully reduced by the ALMA team.

question.value: How does stellar feedback from the young massive super star cluster B1 in the Antennae overlap region act on and disrupt its surrounding molecular gas?

evidence.quote: Based on ALMA and VLT observations, we study this process in a SSC in the overlap region of the Antennae galaxies (22 Mpc)

evidence.quote: This multiplicative factor of 0.5 is found to minimise the dispersion of the residuals after subtracting the water maser contribution

results_numeric.quantity: Radiation pressure P_rad/kB at R_in=35 pc

evidence.quote: \frac{P_{\rm rad}}{k_{\rm B}}=3.4\times 10^{7}\times (1+\langle\tau_{\rm rad}\rangle)
1.2\pm 0.4\times 10^7\times \left(\frac{[35~{\rm pc}]}{R_{\rm in}}\right)^{3/2}
We find that the expansion velocity of the gas is $v_{\rm exp}\sim80$ km s$^{-1}$.
t_{\rm feedback}\simeq R_{\rm high}/v_{\rm exp}\simeq 1.2\,{\rm Myr}
\simeq 30$ $M_{\odot}$/yr
We estimate a lower limit for the SFE within 100 pc from the cluster of 17%
We find R$_{S(1)}=0.32\pm 0.04$ for the low velocity component

findings_qualitative.value: CO has a low velocity component at the cluster and a high velocity bubble-like component around it

evidence.quote: The cluster has two CO velocity components, a low velocity one spatially associated with the cluster and a high velocity one distributed in a bubble-like shape around the cluster.

claims.hypothesis: Radiation pressure disrupted the parent cloud of B1 and the high velocity gas is outflow
claims.experiment: Momentum balance with CO high velocity mass, plus H2 line ratio and Br gamma channel maps
claims.result: 1+tau_rad ~21, t ~1.2 Myr, R_S(1)<0.18, escaping Br gamma
claims.finding: High velocity component likely outflowing parent cloud gas accelerated in ~1 Myr

evidence.quote: We propose that most of the parent cloud has already been blown away, accelerated at the early stages of the SSC evolution by radiation pressure, in a timescale $\sim$1 Myr.

claims.hypothesis: Current radiation pressure can push the molecular gas near B1
claims.result: P_rad weaker than P_grav; hot gas pressure 3x weaker than P_rad
claims.finding: Present radiation pressure cannot disperse the gas; no IR trapping

evidence.quote: It is not strong enough to push away the molecular gas associated with SSC B1.

claims.hypothesis: B1 is bound and will become a globular cluster

evidence.quote: Within $\sim$100 pc from the cluster, we estimate a lower limit for the SFE of 17%, smaller than the theoretical limit of 30% needed to form a bound cluster.

why_this_method.value: Starburst-like X_CO chosen because it agrees with continuum and virial masses

evidence.quote: In this paper we choose to use a starburst-like value, which gives us a good agreement with our other measurements of the molecular gas

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Galactic X_CO would give >3 times higher mass

evidence.quote: the mass would be more than 3 times higher

limitations_admitted.value: Resolution cannot resolve structures smaller than 50 pc; cluster velocity unknown

evidence.quote: With the existing data we cannot resolve structures smaller than 50 pc
